question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of each particle about a fixed axis is:

options.text: Proportional to its distance from the axis

solution:
The correct answer is __**Identical for all particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **angular velocity** of a rigid body is a measure of how fast the body rotates about a fixed axis. It is expressed as a vector quantity, typically denoted by **ω**.
 
• In the case of a **rigid body**, all particles in the body rotate with the same angular velocity about the fixed axis. This property arises due to the rigidity of the body, which ensures no relative motion between particles. *Hence, the correct option is "Identical for all particles."*
 
• The statement "Proportional to its distance from the axis" is incorrect because the angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis; however, the **linear velocity** does depend on the distance from the axis. Linear velocity is given by **v = ωr**, where **r** is the radial distance from the axis.
 
• The statement "Inversely proportional to radius" is incorrect because angular velocity remains constant for all particles in a rigid body, irrespective of their distance from the axis. This property is a fundamental characteristic of rigid body rotation.
 
• The statement "Always constant at zero" is incorrect unless the rigid body is stationary. If the body is rotating, its angular velocity will have a non-zero value.
 
• All particles of a rigid body exhibit **uniform angular velocity**, ensuring synchronized rotation about the axis. This uniformity is critical for applications like gears, turbines, and rotating machinery.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is "Identical for all particles."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Angular Velocity:**

 
 
• **Angular velocity** is defined as the rate of change of angular displacement and is typically measured in radians per second (**rad/s**).
 
• For a rigid body, **angular velocity** is a vector quantity directed along the axis of rotation, following the right-hand rule.
 
 
 
• **Rigid Body Characteristics:**
 
 
• A **rigid body** is an idealized object in which deformation is negligible, and all constituent particles maintain fixed distances relative to each other.
 
• Examples of rigid bodies include gears, wheels, and turbines used in mechanical systems.
 
 
 
• **Key Distinctions:**
 
 
• **Linear velocity (v)** varies for different points on the rigid body and is proportional to the distance from the axis of rotation (**v = ωr**).
 
• **Angular velocity (ω)**, however, remains uniform across all points of the rigid body.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• In machinery, ensuring uniform angular velocity is critical for the efficient functioning of rotating components like turbines, flywheels, and disk drives.
 
• Rotational motion principles are also applied in aerospace engineering for satellite stabilization and gyroscopic systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Formula:**

 
 
• The relationship between **linear velocity** and **angular velocity** is given by **v = ωr**, where **r** is the radial distance from the axis.
 
• For a rigid body, **ω** remains constant across all points, but **v** increases with increasing **r**.
 
 
 
• **Examples in Physics:**
 
 
• In a rotating disk, points closer to the center have lower **linear velocity**, while points near the edge exhibit higher **linear velocity**.
 
• In planetary motion, angular velocity helps describe the rotation of celestial bodies, such as the Earth’s rotation around its axis.
